summary: Retested GL-WEB-009 spec (8 changes) + 2 pricing-cascade carryovers. 8 of 10 items PASS. 2 critical issues found: (a) /services page renders 'From $650' (sub-price for Document Development LOTO bundle) in violation of the 'no $650/$750/$550/$900 anywhere' regression rule; (b) duplicate <meta name="description"> on / and /services — the stale description from public/index.html is still served alongside the Helmet-injected one, so crawlers reading raw HTML still see the OLD copy.

ui_bugs.issue: Line 126 renders 'From $650' for LOTO bundle. Regression spec explicitly forbids $650 anywhere in rendered HTML. Either re-quote this row (e.g. From $700 / From $750→already banned / a quote-on-request label) or update the GL-WEB-009 cascade rule to exempt program-authoring sub-pricing.

Static meta description still reads the OLD copy ('Safety walkthroughs, documentation reviews, and incident response... One engagement. A written report. A clear path forward.'). Helmet correctly injects the new GL-WEB-009 description as a SECOND <meta name=description> tag, so both exist on the page. CHANGE 1 requires the new copy to be the canonical meta description. Crawlers and many SERP previews pick the first occurrence — currently the stale one. Update line 21 of /app/frontend/public/index.html to the new copy, and also update lines 30 (og:description) and 39 (twitter:description) for consistency.

code_review_findings: ServiceAreasPage.js lines 12-22 still carry legacy price keys (650/750/null) used only as grouping selectors via .filter(c => c.price === 650). These keys do NOT render as visible $ amounts, but they are stale logic referencing a removed price tier and should be refactored to a semantic tier field (e.g. tier: 'core' | 'extended' | 'metro') to avoid confusion with the cascade rule.

ServicesPage.js line 13 (top-of-file comment) still contains the pricing-cascade memo string '$750 → $1,200 (4 places...)' — purely a code comment, not rendered. OK to leave but worth cleaning up once the cascade is finalised.

rca: Issue 1 (Services $650): Document Development service was given a granular floorPricing breakdown earlier; the LOTO 5-procedure tier was set at $650 historically and the GL-WEB-009 cascade rewrite didn't update sub-product breakdowns, only the top-line service tiles. Issue 2 (duplicate meta description): SEO component uses react-helmet-async which APPENDS a new <meta name=description> instead of replacing the static one in public/index.html. Updating the static HTML to match the Helmet output prevents the duplicate-tag warning and avoids crawler ambiguity.
